output.brief: The wrong expiry dates were not caused by the operators. From 4 Oct, the data PackBridge sent to the printers carried a 36-month shelf life for Veltranol instead of 24, and the printers printed exactly what they received. No operator overrode anything, and the affected jobs include permanent staff on day shift. The 36-month value traces to a Regulatory Affairs edit entered 3 Oct under CC-309, which was meant to apply only from 1 Mar 2027, yet the value in effect was 36 in October. The ERP still holds 24 as the current value. Before the change, every job was correct, so the firmware change and the agency staff do not explain it. Next: put Veltranol lots packed since 4 Oct on hold, including the two lots already in the warehouse, and correct the Veltranol record so only 24 is used. Ask IT and Corvane to explain why PackBridge used the future-dated value. Check the other products changed under CC-309, especially MR-05-14, before any other action. Do not remove the agency staff or switch off the camera check. I am fairly confident about the cause but not certain of the mechanism.
